title: Crypto Shares Surge as Treasury Doubles Buybacks, Trump Pushes Clarity Act
excerpt: Bitcoin crossed $70,000 for the first time since June after the U.S. Treasury doubled long-duration debt buyback sizes, while Trump urged Congress to pass landmark crypto legislation.
body:
• Cryptocurrency stocks surged after the U.S. Treasury doubled buyback sizes for long-duration debt to at least $4 billion per operation, boosting risk assets
  • Bitcoin crossed $70,000 for the first time since June, rising 3.48% to $71,505, while Ether gained 2.46% to $2,272
  • President Trump urged Congress to pass the Clarity Act, which would define whether crypto qualifies as a security or a commodity
  • The rally was fueled by short-covering after weeks of narrow trading, with Coinbase up 6%, Strategy up 4%, and Canaan surging over 10%

Cryptocurrency-related stocks surged on Thursday after the U.S. Treasury Department doubled its buyback sizes for long-duration debt, sending a positive signal to risk assets, and as President Donald Trump pushed Congress to pass landmark digital-asset legislation.

Bitcoin crossed the $70,000 mark for the first time since June, rising 3.48% to $71,505, according to Reuters. Ether climbed 2.46% to $2,272, its highest level in over three months. The broader crypto market rally spilled into equities, with Coinbase Global gaining 6.05%, bitcoin-focused Strategy rising 4%, and mining hardware maker Canaan surging 10.37%.

Treasury Intervention Lifts Risk Assets

The Treasury's move came after a major bond selloff pushed the 30-year yield to its highest level since 2007 at nearly 5.34%, reflecting growing concerns about inflation and swelling government debt. Long-dated government yields fell by as much as 10 basis points following the announcement.

Under the buyback program, launched in May 2024 to improve liquidity in the $32 trillion Treasury market, the department periodically repurchases older, less liquid outstanding bonds. The doubling of operation sizes — from $2 billion to at least $4 billion — was the first concrete intervention by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to ease pressure on the long end of the yield curve.

"The rally was then fueled by a wave of short-covering, following weeks of extremely narrow trading."

— Alex Kuptsikevich, Chief Market Analyst, FxPro

The retreat in yields also weighed heavily on the dollar, which fell 0.84% against a basket of currencies to 98.80, while spot gold rose 4.05% to $4,508.64 an ounce. The divergence between a weaker dollar and surging hard assets reflects growing unease over the U.S. debt trajectory, according to Reuters.

Trump Pushes Clarity Act

Investors also drew encouragement from Trump's show of support for crypto legislation at a White House event with industry executives on Wednesday. The president, who promised on the campaign trail to make the United States the "crypto capital of the world," called on lawmakers to pass a "fair version of the Clarity Act," currently stalled in the Senate.

The Clarity Act, if enacted, would define whether cryptocurrency qualifies as a security or a commodity, clarifying jurisdiction between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Industry executives and analysts have said that without legislation, regulations remain vulnerable to shifting political winds and court challenges.

"Trump's comments are incrementally positive because they suggest the White House is putting more direct pressure on Congress to get the legislation done."

— Bo Pei, Analyst, U.S. Tiger Securities

However, many Democrats and some Republicans have said they would not support a bill without strong language banning political officials, including Trump, from profiting from their own crypto ventures. Trump disclosed more than $1.4 billion in earnings from his family's crypto ventures in 2025.

Broader Market Context

The crypto rally unfolded against a backdrop of global market jitters. Long-term borrowing costs from the U.S. to Germany and Japan have soared as investors grow anxious about ballooning government debt and elevated inflation, compounded by tensions in the Middle East.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's July meeting, released Wednesday, showed that concern about inflation deepened last month, with several policymakers ready to raise interest rates. Markets now price in a 31% chance of a September rate hike, rising to 65% by December.

What's Next

While the Treasury's intervention offered a lifeline to risk assets, analysts caution the relief may be short-lived. The fundamental pressures driving yields higher — fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, and geopolitical risk — remain in play. For crypto markets, the trajectory of the Clarity Act through Congress and the Fed's next policy moves will be key catalysts in the weeks ahead.

Stablecoin issuer Circle gained 3.8% and retail trading platform Robinhood advanced 0.42%, rounding out a broadly positive session for crypto-linked equities.
